note: The hand-written structure of roadmap-data.json: lane order (keyed by epic WBS and category code, never by issue number), stage names, the program-gate edges that exist only as prose in programs.json tierRelation, pins, wave-window pins and the extra open calls. Every pin and window pin is echoed in roadmap-data.json overlay.applied, so a reader can tell a decision from a computation.
lanesNote: Array order is lane order, so dependency arrows run down and to the right. A tiered item takes the lane of its plan language; everything else takes its category's lane, then its epic's. An epic with no lane raises epic-without-lane and lands in Other: a new epic needs exactly one entry here.

stages.name: Landed
stages.entryCondition: Nothing. This column is what is already true on the integration branch or on main.
stages.exitCondition: Nothing open depends on it. Delivered work that still gates open work is drawn in its tier band instead, with the delivered-unmerged hatch.

stages.name: Parse truth and the seam's base
stages.entryCondition: Nothing: it starts from the landed substrate.
stages.exitCondition: No statement is silently accepted or silently wrong, and the execution package no longer depends on the language package (#1577).

stages.name: The universal rule and the seam split
stages.entryCondition: #1068 is merged; the seam split starts once #1577 has landed.
stages.exitCondition: Every unsupported keyword and stray character is a coded rejection in all three languages, and each model has its own session type (#1578).

stages.name: The execution seam's final names
stages.exitCondition: Every Database.Execution type is a Database* type (#1579): the T1 work writes against the final names.

stages.name: Wire reach
stages.exitCondition: Documents has a wire server and client (#190), so OQL is testable as a consumer.

stages.name: Gate step {n}
stages.entryCondition: The previous gate column has landed.

stages.name: Foundations
stages.entryCondition: #1101 is merged and #1579 has given the execution types their final names; OQL also needs #190 delivered (D5, owner decision 2026-10-16).
stages.exitCondition: The shared parameter, diagnostic and EXPLAIN contracts exist and each language's entry clauses execute.

stages.name: Composition
stages.exitCondition: Joins, predicates, projections and patterns compose with each other.

stages.name: Derivation
stages.exitCondition: Subqueries, casts, function tables, array operators and RETURN work on composed input.

stages.name: Convergence
stages.exitCondition: CTEs, views, constraint actions, partial updates, ordering and linear composition execute.

stages.name: T1 close-out
stages.entryCondition: Convergence holds and SQL #1120 (the T1 function model) is done.
stages.exitCondition: T1 is complete in all three languages.

stages.name: T2 step {n}
stages.entryCondition: T1 is complete for that language; families follow the order the plan lists them (D4). The order positions; it does not block.
stages.exitCondition: Each family built or explicitly dropped.

stages.name: T3 - competitive depth
stages.entryCondition: T2 has been reviewed (D4: T3 deferred, revisit after T2).

stages.name: Unplaced
stages.entryCondition: No Tier, Wave, Priority or recorded dependency. The board has not said when.
stages.exitCondition: Empty: every item has a Tier, a Wave or a Priority, or work that waits on it.

stagesNote: Keyed by band and localDepth. An entry whose localDepth is "*" names every column of that band that has no entry of its own; {n} is localDepth + 1. A computed column with no name at all raises no-stage-name.

programGateEdges.note: E1's engine-owned bound expression tree is the execution substrate every SQL T1 family (#1106-#1125) runs on; drawn once against the SQL T1 feature rather than twenty times.
E2's SQL function ABI is the catalog #1120's 42 T1 scalar functions register into.
E3's cast registry is what #1119 (CAST across every shared type) extends.
E3's SqlTypeCatalog is what #1108 (ISO multi-word type names) extends.
B1's typed-schema and provisioning path is where the T1 constraint-action DDL lands.
B1's typed-schema and provisioning path is where ALTER TABLE / ALTER COLUMN lands.
B1's typed-schema and provisioning path is where IDENTITY lands.
B1's typed-schema and provisioning path is where views land.
P6 removed the root interfaces every model and client names, so the shared language platform lands on the post-P6 shape.
Shared T1 #1103 defines the diagnostic codes; #1350 is what carries one into a traced failure, so it follows #1103.
The Hardening storage feature #1518 picks up where storage step S3 stopped.

waveWindowsNote: Optional pins: "W03": { "bands": ["t2"], "reason": "..." } sets a window to the full span of the named bands instead of the computed calibration. Every pin is echoed in overlay.applied.

openCalls.text: Priority and Wave for the Unplaced items. Realignment decision 14 approved setting both on 2026-10-16; the values are the owner's, and until they are set the items stay Unplaced.

openCallsNote: Open owner calls only. C1 (T2 order per language), C4 (Ready means unblocked), C5 (#190 first) and C6 (#1540, #1522 and #1541 stay flagged, unedited) were decided on 2026-10-16 as realignment decisions 16, 12, 11 and 17; they live in realign-plan.json. C2 and C3 come from bug-policy.json pendingExtensions. "affects": "unplaced" means every item the run leaves in the Unplaced column.

programP8Call.text: Sequence concrete-first P8 (#1264, the per-row result types: QueryRow, QueryResultSet and QueryResult, renamed Database* by #1579) against shared T1 #1104 and SQL T1 #1117, which need the same result types.
